sources.entry: Dayflow - Screen activity timeline with AI support. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/JerryZLiu/Dayflow) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Dayflow is an open-source, local-first macOS app that records screen activity and uses AI to turn your day into a searchable, timeline-based work journal.
summary.what_it_does: Dayflow runs in the background on a Mac and captures lightweight screen chunks, then analyzes them with a chosen AI provider to produce chronological activity cards. It builds a daily timeline, a GitHub-style activity grid, and standup notes covering yesterday's highlights, today's tasks, and blockers. A weekly review summarizes focus patterns, app usage, and distracting sessions. Users can chat with their timeline in natural language and export it as Markdown for any date range. Recordings and the database stay on the Mac by default, and automatic cleanup can purge old recordings based on configured storage limits.
use_cases: Reconstruct what I did on my Mac today
Write daily standup updates from screen activity
Review how my work week was spent
Export a timeline to Markdown for status reports
Ask questions about past work without digging through notes
how_to_run: Download the latest Dayflow.dmg from GitHub Releases, open it, and drag Dayflow into Applications
Grant Screen & System Audio Recording permission when prompted
Or install via Homebrew: brew install --cask dayflow
Build from source: git clone the repository, cd Dayflow, open Dayflow/Dayflow.xcodeproj in Xcode
Select the Dayflow scheme in Xcode and run it
stack: ChatGPT / Claude via local CLI tools (optional)
notable: Local-first storage: recordings, timeline, and database stay in ~/Library/Application Support/Dayflow/ by default
Choice of AI backend: fully local models via Ollama or LM Studio, or cloud providers like Gemini, ChatGPT, or Claude
Context-aware analysis that describes what was on screen rather than just the active app name
Automatic storage cleanup with configurable limits for old recordings
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later and Screen & System Audio Recording permission
If a cloud AI provider is chosen, activity data needed for analysis is sent to that provider
Some AI options require separate setup such as a Gemini API key, Ollama, LM Studio, or CLI tools
